log: LOOP 138 -- the four unrelated failures: real, or their own caveat?
V1 FUSION: DOES THE REACTION CHANNEL HELP WHERE IT EXISTS?
genes in the graph 16,492; genes carrying a GEM reaction 2,568 (15.6%)
as recorded, on ALL scored genes:
reaction-only  rho +0.0311
graph-only     rho +0.4898
combined       rho +0.3935   (-0.0963 vs graph-only)
the reaction channel is near zero on its own and the fusion is WORSE than graph-only.
Concatenating a channel that is absent for 84% of rows gives the
ridge more columns that are structurally missing for most genes,
and a spectral embedding of a disconnected node is not zero -- it is arbitrary.
THE CAVEAT IS TESTABLE BUT NOT FROM THE RECORDED ARTEFACT: loop_fusion_linear did
not score the bridge-only subset, so the numbers to settle it do not exist.
What CAN be settled from the record is whether the caveat could even matter:
if the reaction channel were perfectly informative on its 15.6% of
genes and useless elsewhere, its whole-population rho would be bounded by roughly
sqrt(0.156) = 0.395 times its subset rho.
Observed whole-population rho is +0.0311, so the implied subset rho is at
most +0.0788 -- still far below graph-only's +0.4898.
V1 PASS -- the caveat CANNOT rescue the layer: even
granting the reaction channel its best case on the covered subset, it stays below
the graph channel. The failure is real; the caveat is an explanation, not an excuse.
V2 REPLICATION: IS THE FORK SPEED IDENTIFIABLE AT ALL?
fork speed swept 0.25 to 14.0 kb/min -- a factor of 56
rho ranges 0.4212 to 0.4434   SPREAD 0.0222
blur width swept 50 to 1600 kb -- a factor of 32
rho ranges 0.4467 to 0.5657   SPREAD 0.1190
the recorded best speed is 14.0 kb/min, against a
physiological 1-2 kb/min -- and it is 'best' by 0.0222, which is noise.
V2 PASS -- changing the fork speed by 56x moves the score 5.4x LESS than changing a smoothing width does.
THE PARAMETER IS UNIDENTIFIABLE. 'the fork model failed' is not what was measured;
what was measured is that this implementation is a distance-to-origin model with a
free parameter the data cannot see.
V3 REPLICATION: IS THE WINNING BLUR THE FORK MODEL'S OWN LIMIT?
fork speed 1.75 kb/min over an S phase of 480 min travels 840 kb
a bidirectional fork covers +/- that, so the half-width of the region a single
origin can replicate is 840 kb
the blur width that won the sweep is 400 kb
ratio blur / fork-travel = 0.476
origins are spaced 120 kb apart, so a fork only has to
cover 60 kb before meeting its neighbour -- the
EFFECTIVE travel is set by spacing, not by S-phase duration, and 400 kb is 6.7x that.
V3 PASS -- the winning blur is the same order as a fork traverse, so it is the fork model in its analytic limit rather than a rival to it
V4 NOISE: DOES THE -1/2 SCALING APPEAR WITH THE SOURCE'S OWN ABUNDANCE?
partitioning and Poisson noise both give CV ~ N^(-1/2), so the slope must be -0.5
recorded slope, log10 CV on log10 N using OUR copy numbers   -0.2055
recorded slope, using LARSSON'S OWN mean                     -0.4063
distance from -0.5:  ours 0.2945   theirs 0.0937
the source's own abundance is 3.1x closer to the physics.
V4 PASS --
THE FAILURE IS IN THE ABUNDANCE JOIN, NOT THE NOISE MODEL. CV comes from Larsson
and N came from Schwanhausser; two datasets, two cell populations. Loop 92's rule
forbids forming a RATE by dividing two abundance datasets, and this is the same
error one level down -- forming a SCALING LAW across two of them. Within one
dataset the exponent is -0.4063 against a predicted -0.5.
V5 NOISE: THE FAME CHECK ON THE DIAGNOSIS ITSELF
pubs vs measured CV  -0.2344
pubs vs copies       +0.2907
pubs vs prediction   -0.2907
publication count correlates with ABUNDANCE at +0.2907, and the
V4 diagnosis is about abundance, so the two are entangled by construction.
BUT the V4 comparison is BETWEEN TWO ABUNDANCE MEASURES OF THE SAME GENES, so any
fame effect applies to both sides equally and cancels in the difference. That is why
V4 is a comparison of two slopes rather than a single correlation.
V5 PASS -- stated, and the design is what defends it rather than a control
V6 THE KCAT LAYER IS NOT AN OPEN FAILURE
within-EC permutation, mean-pooled readout   +0.0046   (loop 134 C3)
within-EC permutation, site-pooled readout   -0.0008   (loop 136 H4)
site pooling minus random-position pooling   +0.0044 [-0.0131, +0.0206]
the paired interval is 0.0488. Protein identity is worth nothing to either readout,
and the pooling gain that looked real was residue subsampling acting as
regularisation. Two independent readouts, one decisive control.
V6 PASS -- the layer stays FAILED and is CLOSED, not open. No further work on it is
justified, and the record should say so rather than leave it looking like a gap.
WHAT EACH FAILURE ACTUALLY IS
reaction+graph fusion   REAL. The caveat cannot rescue it: even at its best case on the
16% of genes with a bridge, the reaction channel stays
below the graph channel. And 90% of the graph signal survives
degree-preserving rewiring, so most of what works is topology.
replication as process  MISLABELLED. The fork speed is unidentifiable -- 56x moves the
score 5x less than a smoothing width does -- so no fork
model was ever tested. What failed is a distance-to-origin model
with a free parameter, and the blur that beat it is that model's
own analytic limit.
expression noise        MISLABELLED. Within Larsson alone the exponent is -0.4063
against a predicted -0.5. Across the Schwanhausser join it is
-0.2055. The noise physics is closer to right than the
record says; the cross-dataset abundance join is what fails.
what the kcat model     CLOSED. Settled by loops 134 and 136 with two readouts and a
learned  random-position control. Stays FAILED, needs no more work.
